unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the generalization that women's will settles the moral. It also cuts Mrs. Kuhn's wish that he be civilized rather than Germanized. Both survived in the first draft. The sister now arrives right after the 'robbery and murder' problem without the hinge explaining why she is lucky for him.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Readers can still infer some connection from her being 'hotly Italian'. The plan does not list the bridge sentence as essential.

evidence.quote: Women have, commonly, a very positive moral sense; that which they will, is right; that which they reject, is wrong; and their will, in most cases, ends by settling the moral.
She saw no gain in helping her brother to be Germanized, and she wanted him much to be civilized.
In July, 1859, she was at Thun in Switzerland, and there Henry Adams joined them. Mrs. Kuhn not only adored Italy

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Women have, commonly, a very positive moral sense…settling the moral' sentence after 'joined them'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Planning omission. The plan protects her description and the woman law but not the moral bridge that links them to the dilemma.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The causal turn from an unsolvable moral question to letting a woman drive is lost. 'Luckily' reads as a vague transition, and the later law ('no woman had ever driven him wrong') loses its moral grounding. The Italian-over-German reorientation also loses its motive.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'Luckily for him' no longer answers the moral dilemma

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft had already cut the 'just judgments of an outraged God' moral. The revision then drops the clause about youth assuming everything had a cause and nature tended to an end. Rome becomes merely 'seductive', and the later 'No law of progress applied to it' loses the expectation it frustrates.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V4 and the 'scheme of evolution' sentences in paragraph 18 still carry part of the idea.

evidence.quote: taking for granted that everything had a cause, and that nature tended to an end, Rome was altogether the most violent vice in the world
To young men seeking education in a serious spirit, taking for granted that everything had a cause, and that nature tended to an end
For the rest, Italy was mostly an emotion and the emotion naturally centred in Rome. Rome before 1870 was seductive beyond resistance.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinstate the first draft's 'To young men seeking education in a serious spirit…most violent vice in the world' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required. The essential list says Rome 'resists any law of progress or sequence'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The argument that Rome is anti-education for a mind expecting sequence, which is central to Ara Coeli and the later dynamic theory, is now asserted rather than set up.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Rome's 'vice' loses its premise of cause and end

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'The thought of posing for a Gibbon never entered his mind. He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness.' It also cuts 'No one ever had answered the question…'. The paragraph now opens on the generalization about great men, and V7 follows the beggar image without the line that makes the question universal and unresolved.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The 'tourist' referent still resolves via 'Sir, I am a tourist!', and V6 and V7 survive intact.

evidence.quote: The thought of posing for a Gibbon never entered his mind. He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness
No one ever had answered the question to the satisfaction of any one else. Substitute the word America for the word Rome
Even the greatest of men cannot sit with dignity among the ruins of the Capitol unless they have something quite original to say about it

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the two first-draft sentences that open paragraph 20 and the 'No one ever had answered' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required section (Rome, Gibbon, Ara Coeli). These sentences support V6 and V7.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The retrospective irony goes flat: the old narrator sees a Gibbon pose that the young tourist did not. The escalation to 'the question became personal' also loses its intermediate step.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Ara Coeli loses the young man's unawareness and the unanswered-question frame

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft dropped the claim that such impressions have economic value. The revision also cuts 'Life had no richer impression to give…' and 'puzzle a Berlin jurist'. 'One's ideas become hopelessly mixed' now follows 'ends attained' directly, so the leap to exchangeable value and equivalents is unprepared.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The essential 'ends attained' idea and the pleasure/pain remark remain.

evidence.quote: Exactly what they teach would puzzle a Berlin jurist; yet they seem to have an economic value
Life had no richer impression to give; it offers barely half-a-dozen such, and the intervals seem long.
but one of the ends attained. One's ideas become hopelessly mixed in trying to reduce such forms of education to a standard of exchangeable value

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Life had no richer impression…' and 'Exactly what they teach would puzzle a Berlin jurist;' before the 'ideas become hopelessly mixed' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required. The essential list says to include the pleasure/pain equivalent remark.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Adams's mock-economic reasoning loses its ascent. The pleasure/pain punchline arrives with less logic and less comic timing.
unresolved_should_improve.title: The Milan equivalents argument jumps without its premise

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the Frau Hofrathin's 'huge laughter' at the young American's helplessness. It also cuts 'He was as ignorant as a schoolboy of society' from the tally. Both were in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The essentials 'There were no accidents in Dresden' and the career tally survive.

evidence.quote: The Frau Hofrathin herself was sometimes roused to huge laughter at the total discomfiture and helplessness of the young American
He had made no step towards a profession. He was as ignorant as a schoolboy of society.
His social failure was humiliating and he succumbed to it. Adams admitted himself unable to guess what use his second winter in Germany was to him.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the Frau Hofrathin laughter sentence and the 'ignorant as a schoolboy of society' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required. The essential list includes the social failure at the Frau Hofrathin's and the tally.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The one comic image of the second winter disappears. The tally's social item, which pairs with 'no profession', is gone.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Dresden social failure stated but not shown
